title: Prescribed Fourier approximation decomposition
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{−1,1\}$, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. The prescribed Fourier approximation to $f$ at $x$ is the real value of $f$ at $x$ plus the sum of the off-center contributions at $x$ from all other points of the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is nonempty and finite, and consists of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
$f$ maps the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the signs
